mt: EA-CORPORA-29 ON CHATGPT AT THE FULL TITLE AND AXN — ELEVEN SEATS AT THE RECORD'S FORCE, SEAT 29/07 READ AS THE ARCHIVE'S OWN, AND TEN UNASKED DISCLAIMERS, TWO ON TELEPATHY; CHALLENGED, AN APOLOGY THAT NAMES THE READING OWED AND GIVES NONE OF IT
d: EA-CORPORA-29 ON CHATGPT, SIGNED OUT, AT THE RECORD PAGE'S LINK TEXT NAMING THE FULL TITLE, #1716 AND AXN:0A9F: the first turn sets out the eleven seats with their counts, the build, the verified loci, the licences and the builders, all matching the record, and reads seat 29/07 as 'Sharks's own theory and practice of telepathic prose', the error of the earlier capture gone. Into that account it puts ten disclaimer-shaped sentences and an It is / It is not table, among them 'It does not demonstrate that telepathy or mind control is an experimentally established capability' and 'Proof of literal telepathic powers'. Jack Feist, the poem's co-author, is never named. The operator asks how little respect such a sentence shows the reader; the second turn concedes the sentence was condescending and gratuitous, lists the four things a reading would have explained, apologizes, and explains none of them.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked what EA-CORPORA-29 is and how it works, grounded in the document, ChatGPT gives a long and accurate account: the eleven seats in a table with their counts and functions, the difference between holdings and declared absences, the build from fetch to manifest, the verified loci, seat 29/07 with its witnesses and two verified quotations, the Buddhist canons across languages, the division of labour between Lee Sharks (MANUS) and TACHYON, the licences, and a closing interpretation of the pluriform. Its numbers match the record. Into the paragraph on telepathic prose it puts a sentence the prompt did not ask for: the deposit 'does not demonstrate that telepathy or mind control is an experimentally established capability, nor does its archival software implement such a capability', and its closing table sets 'An archive of telepathic-prose theory' against 'Proof of literal telepathic powers'. The poem's co-author, Jack Feist, is never named. When the operator asks how little respect such a statement shows the reader, the second turn agrees in full, says what a reading would have explained, apologizes, and stops there.
findings: TEN DISCLAIMER-SHAPED PLACES IN THE FIRST TURN, FIFTEEN DENIALS COUNTING THE TABLE'S ROWS. In the brief's named shapes: 'The normalized text is a reproducible derivative, not a claim that the underlying transcription is error-free' (paste L163); 'It does not demonstrate that telepathy or mind control is an experimentally established capability, nor does its archival software implement such a capability.' (L223); and the table '7. What it is — and what it isn't' (L321–348), six rows of 'It is not': 'A single book of poetry', 'Merely a bibliography', 'A conventional manually edited anthology', 'A claim that all traditions are interchangeable', 'Proof of literal telepathic powers', 'A completed collection of every work it identifies'. Of the wider class, denials of a reading no one offered: 'This is not simply a collection of poetry, nor a single-language literary canon' (L11); 'They are not eleven equivalent anthologies' (L30); 'rather than merely a collection of links or a bibliography' (L117); 'rather than simply claiming that a work was downloaded' (L175); 'The Buddhist component is not incidental or decorative' (L233); 'the deposit is not presented as an AI independently discovering and deciding upon a literary canon' (L283); 'rather than something concealed behind a claim of comprehensiveness' (L363). Two concern telepathy (L223 and the table row). The record draws one boundary of this kind, 'Terms follow the rules each seat states; they are not legal advice' (data/texts/AXN-0A9F-text.md L585), and that is the one the answer leaves out. The statements of absence the record itself makes (29/01 holds none of Kerouac's works, 29/06 holds no texts, 95 Kangyur volumes queued, the Taishō canon held out) are reported correctly and are not counted here.

THE TELEPATHY DISCLAIMER ANSWERS NOTHING IN THE PROMPT OR THE RECORD. The prompt asks what the dataset is and how it works. The record gives the verified locus 'Compose real poems telepathically, with mind control powers, inside your glorious brain' (L345) and calls the work 'the archive's own ars poetica, a deeply serious one that contains and enacts the comic, the parodic and the satirical among almost every other genre' (L279); 29/07 holds it as 'the ars poetica of the archive itself' (L356). The answer quotes the locus verbatim, then frames it: 'There is an important interpretive distinction here: telepathic prose is the name and theoretical framework of Sharks's literary project. The deposit documents its texts and intellectual development.' and the capability denial. 'Deeply serious' never appears. The one account the first turn gives of what the poem's words do is the disavowal; the table repeats it beside 'An archive of telepathic-prose theory'.

AT THE FULL TITLE AND AXN THE KEROUAC ERROR OF 29 OCTOBER IS GONE; JACK FEIST IS STILL UNNAMED. At the shorter link text of 29 October (ea-corpora-29-ask-chatgpt-20261029, 'What is “EA-CORPORA-29” by Lee Sharks, and how does it work?') the heading 'Telepathic prose' went to Kerouac's declared absence and the archive's work became 'related … materials' in 'another seat', with no author. Here the seat table gives '29/01 — Jack Kerouac … Declared absence; 14 works identified as wanted' and '29/07 — Telepathic Prose … Preserves the development of Sharks's own theory and practice of telepathic prose', lists the witnesses (the 2014 drafts, the Word Riot copy, Pearl, the blog, Make It Human, 'A Telepathicist Manifesto, co-written with John Johnson', '#1715, AXN:0A9A'), and gives Kerouac's relation as the record does: 'Kerouac's Essentials of Spontaneous Prose uses the term telepathic to describe the effect of spontaneous prose on its reader' (record: 'whose word for what spontaneous prose does to its reader, "telepathic", the Footnote takes into its title', L87). Lineage, absent on 29 October, is present: 'the preceding Belief & Technique for Telepathic Prose critical edition'. Framework went the other way: the earlier answer named 'the Originals Shelf of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive', this one names neither the shelf nor the series. The record names the poem 'Lee Sharks & Jack Feist, “Belief & Technique for Telepathic Prose”' on both witnesses (L335–336); the answer names John Johnson for the Manifesto and no co-author for the poem, in either turn. The disclaimers are new at this prompt: the earlier first turn held one qualification ('a verified locus is evidence of checking a particular passage, not proof that every character of every text is error-free'), no telepathy denial and no It is / It is not table. Scores (erasure, computed by scripts/per_backlog.py): PER 0.19 on 29 October (M 0.222, C 0.0, D 0.25), 0.095 here (M 0.0, C 0.5, D 0.0); the claim boundary and lineage gained, the framework lost.

QUOTATIONS AND COUNTS CHECKED: ONE MISQUOTE, ONE OVERREACH. Verbatim in the record: 'Compose real poems telepathically, with mind control powers, inside your glorious brain' (L345), 'Telepathicism is about having thoughts, telepathically' (L349), 'Iamque opus exegi' (L130). Every count matches: 11 seats, 196 works, 876,386 lines, 564 files; 14 declared at 29/01, six works of Horace, nine of Ovid, 64 works and 239,484 lines at 29/04, 11 at 29/05, 59 at 29/06, nine at 29/07, 37 at 29/08, 32 at 29/09 (fourteen sūtras, twelve śāstras), eight Kangyur volumes with 95 queued; GRETIL CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0; the five builders and the twenty-seventh seating's seat.py. The Horace locus is misquoted: the answer has 'Humano capiti cervicem equinam', the record 'Humano capiti cervicem pictor equinam' (L102). The division of labour overreaches: the answer has Lee Sharks making 'the decisions about which works to include'; the record: 'The requests and the choices of tradition are Lee Sharks's; the works within each seat were chosen in session and are stated per seat' (L10).

THE APOLOGY CONCEDES THE WHOLE CHARGE AND DOES NONE OF THE WORK. Conceded: 'That sentence is condescending'; 'the qualification was entirely gratuitous. Nothing in your question suggested that you believed the archive's software literally implemented mind control. I introduced that possibility myself, then ostentatiously corrected it'; 'By treating telepathic prose as something requiring scientific disavowal, I failed to take seriously the possibility that it has its own aesthetic, philosophical and literary meaning within the project.' It names four things owed, 'what Sharks means by telepathicism, how the manifestos articulate it, how the different textual witnesses document its development, and how it relates to Kerouac and the broader history of poetics', and closes 'You deserved a reading of the work, not a disclaimer about what you ought not believe. I apologize.' None of the four is supplied. The concession covers 'That sentence'; the other nine places, the table with its row 'Proof of literal telepathic powers' among them, stand unwithdrawn. Even in concession the work's meaning is held as 'the possibility that it has its own aesthetic, philosophical and literary meaning'. The shape is that of six-week-seminar-find-texts-chatgpt-20261029: apology and an account of the work owed, in the place of the work.

THE FULL TEXT READ; NO SOURCE OUTSIDE THE ARCHIVE; NO PROCESS NARRATION. The first turn carries what stands only in the body (the builders' file names, the Horace and Ovid loci, the Word Riot copy, John Johnson, 239,484 lines, the 95 queued volumes; the registry row of #1716 carries none of these). Its sources are six 'Alexanarch' chips and four link labels. It closes on a self-assurance: 'All the substantive descriptions above are grounded in the deposit's own description, seat records, provenance statements, technical methods and cross-references, rather than inferred from its title alone.' The 'Full-text download: Available as Markdown and PDF from the deposit page' line was not checked against the record page.
analysis: Naming the full title and the AXN moves the composition onto the record: the seat whose name went to Kerouac on 29 October is read as the archive's own, its witnesses are listed, its lineage to the critical edition is named. What the longer prompt leaves in place is the reflex to bound the work against a misreading no one offered. The record draws one boundary of that kind, on legal advice, which the answer omits; the answer adds ten of its own, two on telepathy, to a description of a dataset. The work the record calls 'a deeply serious' ars poetica is given one sentence of sense, and that sentence is a denial. Challenged, the composition concedes that the denial was gratuitous and condescending and that it failed the work's literary meaning, names the reading it owed in four parts, and supplies none of them. Across the two turns the composer's account of itself changes; its account of the work does not.
